title: Netscape Navigator Web Browser
summary: The dominant web browser of the mid-1990s that introduced JavaScript, frames, cookies, and SSL encryption to the World Wide Web.
facts: Created by Marc Andreessen and Jim Clark, built upon NCSA Mosaic concepts.
Netscape Communications went public in 1995, triggering the dot-com boom.
Introduced JavaScript (initially called LiveScript) created by Brendan Eich.

title: America Online (AOL)
summary: The ubiquitous online service provider famous for dial-up internet access, direct-mail CD-ROMs, chat rooms, Instant Messenger, and 'You've Got Mail!'.
facts: Distributed millions of free trial CD-ROMs in magazines, mailboxes, and cereal boxes.
Used proprietary Keyword navigation system (e.g. AOL Keyword: MOVIES).
Elwood Edwards provided the iconic voice for 'You've Got Mail'.

title: GeoCities Web Hosting
summary: Popular web hosting service that organized personal websites into thematic neighborhoods like SiliconValley, Hollywood, and Area51.
facts: Featured custom HTML, animated GIF banners, under construction icons, and MIDI background music.
Acquired by Yahoo! in 1999 for $3.57 billion at the height of the dot-com bubble.
Pioneered user-generated web content and personal homepage culture.

title: AltaVista Search Engine
summary: Pioneering web search engine known for fast full-text web crawler indexing and boolean search operators.
facts: Developed by researchers at DEC Network Systems Laboratory in Palo Alto.
Indexed over 20 million web pages in 1995 using powerful 64-bit Alpha processors.
Introduced Babel Fish multilingual automatic translation service.

title: ICQ Instant Messenger
summary: The first major standalone real-time internet instant messaging service, famous for UIN numbers and its iconic 'Uh-oh!' notification sound.
facts: Created by Israeli company Mirabilis founded by Yair Goldfinger, Arik Vardi, Sefi Vigiser, and Amnon Amir.
Assigned numeric User Identification Numbers (UINs) to all subscribers.
Acquired by AOL in 1998 for $407 million.
